domain.name: Construction & Trades
domain.description: Practical construction planning, measurement, drawings, estimating, tools, structural awareness, site safety, and weatherproofing fundamentals.

competencies.name: Measurement & Layout
competencies.description: Measure, mark, square, level, and transfer dimensions accurately.
competencies.purpose: Reduce fit errors and cumulative layout drift.

units.title: Small layout errors compound
units.content: Repeated cuts and offsets can amplify a small measurement error across a wall, platform, cabinet run, or finish system.

units.title: Measure-mark-verify workflow
units.content: Confirm reference edge and units; measure twice from a stable datum; mark clearly; verify square, level, or plumb as required; account for material thickness and kerf; then cut or fasten only after the layout is checked.

units.title: Layout failures
units.content: Avoid chaining dimensions from previous marks, mixing units, measuring from damaged edges, and cutting before checking orientation and thickness.

drills.title: Lay out a small platform
drills.prompt: Explain the measurement and verification sequence for laying out a rectangular platform frame from a drawing.

competencies.name: Drawing & Plan Reading
competencies.description: Interpret dimensions, symbols, sections, notes, and relationships in basic construction drawings.
competencies.purpose: Translate design intent into coordinated field work.

units.title: Drawings are coordinated views, not isolated pictures
units.content: Plans, elevations, sections, details, schedules, and notes each reveal different information and must be read together.

units.title: Plan reading order
units.content: Check title, scale, revision, legend, and general notes; identify grid or reference points; review plan, elevation, and section relationships; follow detail callouts; then verify dimensions and conflicts before work.

units.title: Plan-reading failures
units.content: Avoid scaling a drawing when written dimensions exist, using an outdated revision, ignoring notes, and assuming a detail applies everywhere without checking callouts.

drills.title: Review a room renovation plan
drills.prompt: Describe how to review a plan set for dimensions, sections, finish notes, door locations, and conflicting information before work begins.

competencies.name: Material Takeoff & Estimating
competencies.description: Estimate quantities, waste, labor assumptions, and cost from defined scope.
competencies.purpose: Support pricing, purchasing, and planning with transparent assumptions.

units.title: Takeoff workflow
units.content: Define scope and units; measure required areas, lengths, or counts; convert to purchasable units; add justified waste; identify accessories and consumables; price using current supplier data; document exclusions and assumptions.

units.title: Separate quantity error from price uncertainty
units.content: Keep measured quantity, waste factor, unit price, and labor assumptions distinct so revisions can be traced.

units.title: Estimating failures
units.content: Avoid forgetting trim, fasteners, adhesives, disposal, delivery, and access constraints; do not hide contingency inside quantities without labeling it.

drills.title: Build a drywall takeoff
drills.prompt: Create the structure of a takeoff for a small room including board, fasteners, compound, tape, corner bead, waste, and delivery assumptions.

competencies.name: Hand & Power Tool Fundamentals
competencies.description: Select and use common tools with basic control, setup, and safety awareness.
competencies.purpose: Match the tool to the task without bypassing guards or safe operating limits.

units.title: Tool capability does not equal permission or competence
units.content: Knowing what a saw, drill, grinder, nailer, or other tool can do does not authorize unsafe use; manufacturer guidance, guarding, PPE, stable workholding, and competent supervision remain controlling.

units.title: Pre-use tool check
units.content: Confirm the correct tool and accessory; inspect power source, guards, fasteners, blade/bit, and damage; secure the work; clear the cut or strike path; use required PPE; then stop if setup or material behavior is uncertain.

units.title: Tool safety failures
units.content: Never defeat guards, use damaged cords or accessories, hold unstable work by hand near a cutting path, exceed accessory ratings, or improvise a tool for a task it was not designed to perform.

drills.title: Choose tools for a repair
drills.prompt: Choose appropriate tools for measuring, fastening, cutting trim, and drilling while identifying the pre-use safety checks for each.

competencies.name: Framing & Load Awareness
competencies.description: Understand basic framing roles and recognize when structural work requires qualified design or inspection.
competencies.purpose: Avoid treating structural members like ordinary finish materials.

units.title: Load path matters
units.content: Walls, joists, beams, posts, headers, connections, and foundations may participate in carrying gravity or lateral loads; removing or altering them can change the structure beyond the visible area.

units.title: Structural-change screening
units.content: Before altering framing, identify whether the element may be load-bearing or bracing; review plans and field conditions; stop when uncertain; obtain qualified structural guidance where required before cutting, drilling, removing, or relocating structural members.

units.title: Structural failures
units.content: Do not assume a wall is nonbearing from appearance alone, cut unknown joists or trusses for utilities, or rely on rule-of-thumb sizing for structural modifications.

drills.title: Screen a proposed wall removal
drills.prompt: List the questions and evidence needed before deciding whether an interior wall can be altered.

competencies.name: Site Safety, Ladders & Access
competencies.description: Recognize fall, housekeeping, access, and work-zone hazards.
competencies.purpose: Reduce preventable injury during construction and maintenance work.

units.title: Work-area safety scan
units.content: Identify fall exposure, ladder/access condition, overhead hazards, electrical hazards, trip paths, dust/noise, public exposure, material storage, and emergency access before work starts.

units.title: Access equipment has limits
units.content: Ladders and temporary access must match the task, height, load, angle, surface, and duration; they are not substitutes for proper platforms or fall protection where those are required.

units.title: Access failures
units.content: Avoid standing on unstable furniture, overreaching from ladders, placing ladders on loose surfaces, blocking exits, and working at height when the access method is not appropriate.

drills.title: Plan safe ceiling access
drills.prompt: Assess a high-ceiling repair and decide what access and hazard controls must be resolved before work begins.

competencies.name: Moisture & Weatherproofing Fundamentals
competencies.description: Understand how bulk water, vapor, drainage, and penetrations affect buildings.
competencies.purpose: Avoid repairs that trap moisture or redirect water into assemblies.

units.title: Water management follows layers and paths
units.content: Roofs, flashing, drainage planes, sealants, penetrations, and ventilation work as a system; visible interior damage may be far from the entry point.

units.title: Moisture diagnosis
units.content: Identify when and where moisture appears; distinguish active leak, condensation, plumbing, and exterior entry possibilities; trace likely paths; inspect upstream transitions; correct the source before cosmetic repair.

units.title: Moisture repair failures
units.content: Avoid sealing wet assemblies closed, caulking over drainage paths, painting over unresolved moisture, and assuming the nearest visible stain is the source.

drills.title: Diagnose a window-area leak
drills.prompt: Create a non-destructive diagnostic sequence for water appearing below a window after heavy rain.

competencies.name: Construction Sequencing & Trade Coordination
competencies.description: Order work so one trade does not damage or block another.
competencies.purpose: Reduce rework and protect finished work.

units.title: Sequence follows dependencies and access
units.content: Rough work, inspections, closures, finishes, fixtures, and punch work have dependencies; the cheapest sequence on paper may fail if access or cure time is ignored.

units.title: Trade coordination plan
units.content: Map scope by trade; identify prerequisite rough-ins and inspections; reserve access; account for drying or cure times; protect completed work; schedule finish work after disruptive work; then verify punch items before demobilization.

units.title: Sequencing failures
units.content: Avoid closing walls before required inspections, installing finishes before dusty work, scheduling trades without access, and omitting protection for completed surfaces.

drills.title: Sequence a small renovation
drills.prompt: Sequence demolition, framing, rough utilities, inspection, drywall, paint, flooring, trim, fixtures, and punch work.
